medications.purpose: Blood pressure control (first‑line per NICE NG136)
medications.nice_justification: NG136 step 1: ACE‑inhibitor recommended for hypertension in adults <55 y or non‑Afro‑Caribbean patients

medications.duration: Indefinite — review BP after 4 weeks and then 6‑12 monthly
medications.purpose: Add‑on therapy to achieve BP target <140/90 mmHg (step 2 combination therapy)
medications.nice_justification: NG136 step 2: ACE‑I + CCB combination when BP uncontrolled on monotherapy

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive blood pressure lowering effect; risk of symptomatic hypotension
interactions_checked.action: Monitor BP within 2 weeks of initiation and advise patient to rise slowly; adjust dose if needed

contraindications.reason: ACE‑I are teratogenic and contraindicated in pregnancy (NG136)
contraindications.alternative: If patient is pregnant, switch to labetalol 100 mg twice daily or methyldopa

Serum potassium not provided – check before adding thiazide‑like diuretic in future

treatment_summary: Patient is on lisinopril 10 mg daily but BP remains 151/105 mmHg. Per NICE NG136, add amlodipine 5 mg daily as second‑line combination therapy. Monitor BP after 2‑4 weeks and renal function/electrolytes at baseline and after any dose change. Confirm pregnancy status and renal function; calculate QRISK and address lifestyle factors (salt <6 g/day, DASH diet, weight loss, exercise, smoking cessation). If BP remains uncontrolled after 4‑6 weeks, consider adding indapamide 1.5 mg daily with potassium monitoring.
